cloud-workspace-from-phone.title: How I want to work from a phone
cloud-workspace-from-phone.summary: I want my phone to become the entry point for work: give instructions through conversation, let AI execute in the cloud, and open a cloud desktop when I need to work directly. A server, a cloud desktop and shared working materials are the foundation I am building.

outsource-capabilities-own-context.title: Capabilities can be outsourced; AI context cannot
outsource-capabilities-own-context.summary: AI has reduced the effort of analysis and writing, but people still maintain continuity: making business decisions, coordinating AI, moving information and checking results.

anthropic-economic-futures.title: Anthropic: what might our economic future look like?
anthropic-economic-futures.summary: Starting from Anthropic's three economic scenarios, I examine how AI may affect growth, work and income distribution, and why a richer economy does not necessarily benefit everyone.

enterprise-and-personal-anc.title: Enterprise and personal ANC: one architecture for organizing AI work around goals
enterprise-and-personal-anc.summary: Enterprises and individuals operate at different scales, but share the same question: how can goals, context, working methods and available capabilities be organized so AI understands what to do and keeps making progress?

personal-organizational-efficiency-ai-pr.title: Personal productivity, organizational productivity and AI products solve different problems
personal-organizational-efficiency-ai-pr.summary: Personal productivity, organizational productivity and AI products address distinct problems: expanding individual capability, changing organizational collaboration and redesigning how a problem is solved.

ai-changes-work-itself.title: AI may change work itself, not just efficiency
ai-changes-work-itself.summary: AI brings more than efficiency gains. As execution and coordination become cheaper, roles, workflows and the boundary between thinking and doing are worth redesigning.

how-ai-may-reshape-recruiting.title: How AI might reshape recruiting
how-ai-may-reshape-recruiting.summary: As AI changes the cost of information access, talent sourcing, capability assessment and communication, how might recruiting roles, responsibilities and business models change?

do-not-let-means-replace-ends.title: Don't let means replace ends: keep your destination in view
do-not-let-means-replace-ends.summary: Completing a means does not guarantee achieving an end. Individuals and companies need to keep checking goals, direction and actual outcomes while taking action.

when-ai-no-longer-needs-human-work.title: When AI no longer needs human work, power becomes the real question
when-ai-no-longer-needs-human-work.summary: As AI moves from assisting humans to organizing production independently, work is not the only thing changing: enterprises, states, resource distribution and the basis of human value may change too.

designing-agent-environment-harness.title: How should we design the environment around a model that can act?
designing-agent-environment-harness.summary: Agent products need more than longer prompts: models need observable, actionable, verifiable and constrained environments. Starting from a real conversational mistake, this article explores responsibilities across skills, tools, harnesses, CLI and LangGraph.

ai-native-product-rewrites-interaction.title: Eating is the goal; ordering delivery is a means: how AI-native products may rewrite interaction
ai-native-product-rewrites-interaction.summary: An AI-native product does not merely replace buttons with chat. It reorganizes context, workflows, confirmation and execution around user goals, removing unnecessary interaction.

product-manager-understand-business-proc.title: How good product managers quickly understand business workflows
product-manager-understand-business-proc.summary: Understanding workflows quickly means more than researching an industry and collecting requests. It requires a product judgement framework around value streams, real tasks, costs and priorities.

ai-native-process.title: AI-native does not eliminate processes; it removes the need to operate them manually
ai-native-process.summary: AI-native is more than replacing buttons with chat: software should understand human work and move workflow operations behind the scenes.

fde-nine-grid-ai-project.title: The FDE nine-part framework: from unclear requirements to a deliverable AI project
fde-nine-grid-ai-project.summary: The FDE nine-part framework connects sales, product and engineering approaches to client types, turning vague AI productivity requests into assessable, deliverable projects.

skill-design-superpowers-fde-skills.title: A skill should be more than a longer prompt: design lessons from Superpowers and FDE Skills
skill-design-superpowers-fde-skills.summary: A skill should be more than a longer prompt. It should provide composable, maintainable behavioral constraints designed around work stages and failure modes.

ai-workflow-fde-lessons.title: Nine FDE lessons from an AI workflow proposal
ai-workflow-fde-lessons.summary: Lessons from analyzing an enterprise AI workflow proposal: scope decisions, validation objectives, delivery rhythm and implementation.

ai-training-and-fde-delivery.title: Enterprise AI: training builds understanding; FDE delivers implementation
ai-training-and-fde-delivery.summary: AI training can build understanding and inspire ideas, but real implementation needs an FDE to diagnose workflows, identify opportunities and deliver a verifiable feedback loop.

rethinking-product-ux-ui-with-ai.title: How can someone without a design background work with AI to get design right?
rethinking-product-ux-ui-with-ai.summary: This made me reconsider two questions: what exactly are product design, UX and UI each responsible for? And when I do not understand design, how should I work with AI to get it right?
